subject: Change default constructor to leave divider unitialized
perf_evidence: Commit message says the change avoids unnecessary work when creating arrays of dividers.
change_summary: The C++ divider default constructor stops initializing its divisor to one.

units.name: public C++ default-constructed signed-64 divider used for division
units.evidence: Alive2 old->new gives a concrete target-more-poisonous counterexample at x=3: old returns 3, new returns poison. The reverse check succeeds.

units.name: default construct then assign a divisor before dividing
units.evidence: Both target_default_then_assign and target_array_init are bidirectionally correct with unroll 4.

notes: This is an intentional C++ API contract change. Only representative signed-64 and initialized unsigned divider paths were checked; the single API counterexample is sufficient to refute full equivalence. O2/O3 optimize the undefined path away, so the O1 witness is decisive for this compiled configuration only. The wrapper disables unchanged x86 inline assembly on both sides.
